ptsd.name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
validationStatements: Your nervous system learned to protect you. These responses kept you alive.
Flashbacks are memories that haven't been processed yet. They're not happening now.
Hypervigilance made sense when you weren't safe. Your body is still checking.
Avoidance is your mind trying to protect you from pain. It's not weakness.

cptsd.name: Complex PTSD
validationStatements: Complex trauma changes how we see ourselves and the world. That's not your fault.
When the people who should have protected you hurt you, it makes sense that trust is hard.
The shame you carry belongs to those who harmed you, not to you.
Your difficulty with emotions makes sense - you never had someone to help you learn to regulate.

did_osdd.name: Dissociative Identity Disorder / OSDD
validationStatements: Your mind created parts to survive what no child should have to survive. That's not disorder - that's adaptation.
All parts are welcome here. All parts have a purpose.
Losing time is disorienting. You're not crazy. Your system is doing its best.
Internal conflict between parts makes sense. You're learning to work together.

bpd.name: Borderline Personality Disorder
validationStatements: Your emotions are intense because you feel things deeply. That's not a flaw.
Fear of abandonment makes sense when you've been left before.
Not knowing who you are is painful. Your identity was shaped by chaos.
The urge to hurt yourself is trying to help you cope with unbearable pain.
keyPhrases: I don't know who I am

depression.name: Major Depressive Disorder
validationStatements: Depression lies to you. It tells you nothing will ever change. That's the illness talking.
Not being able to feel pleasure isn't laziness. Your brain's reward system is struggling.
The exhaustion is real. Depression takes enormous energy to carry.
Feeling worthless is a symptom, not a truth about who you are.

anxiety_disorders.name: Anxiety Disorders
validationStatements: Your anxiety is your brain trying to protect you from perceived threats.
Panic attacks are terrifying but not dangerous. Your body thinks there's danger when there isn't.
The physical symptoms are real. Anxiety lives in the body.
Avoiding things that scare you makes sense, even when it shrinks your world.

ocd.name: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
validationStatements: Intrusive thoughts are not who you are. Everyone has them - OCD just makes them stick.
The compulsions make sense - they temporarily relieve unbearable anxiety.
Needing certainty in an uncertain world is exhausting. OCD exploits that need.
The guilt you feel about your thoughts is part of the disorder, not evidence of your character.

eating_disorders.name: Eating Disorders
validationStatements: Your relationship with food and your body developed for reasons that made sense.
Control over food often starts when other things feel out of control.
The shame around eating is not about food - it's about deeper pain.
Your body is not the enemy, even when it feels that way.

bipolar.name: Bipolar Disorder
validationStatements: Your brain cycles between states. Neither state is the 'real' you - you are all of it.
Mania can feel amazing until it doesn't. The crash is not your fault.
Managing bipolar takes enormous effort. You're doing hard work.
The impulsivity during episodes doesn't define your character.

schizophrenia_spectrum.name: Schizophrenia Spectrum
validationStatements: What you're experiencing is real to you, even if others can't perceive it.
Your brain processes information differently. That's not a moral failing.
The voices or visions are distressing. You don't have to face them alone.
Paranoia often starts from real experiences of being unsafe or betrayed.

autism.name: Autism Spectrum
validationStatements: Your brain processes the world differently. That's neurodiversity, not disorder.
Masking to fit in is exhausting. You deserve spaces where you can be yourself.
Meltdowns and shutdowns are your nervous system's response to overwhelm, not bad behavior.
Your need for routine and predictability is valid.

adhd.name: ADHD
validationStatements: Your brain works differently, not deficiently. ADHD has strengths too.
Rejection sensitivity is real and painful. Your reactions make sense.
Time blindness isn't laziness. Your brain genuinely perceives time differently.
The shame from years of 'not trying hard enough' isn't deserved.

grief.name: Grief and Loss
validationStatements: Grief has no timeline. There's no right way to grieve.
The waves of pain are normal. Grief comes and goes.
Missing them doesn't mean you're not healing. Love doesn't end.
Anger at the person who died, or at yourself, is a normal part of grief.

substance_use.name: Substance Use
validationStatements: Substances often start as a solution to unbearable pain. You were trying to survive.
Relapse is part of recovery for many people. It doesn't erase your progress.
The shame around addiction often makes it harder to get help. You deserve compassion.
Craving is your brain, not your character. You're fighting neurobiology.

active_suicidal_plan.languageGuidance: CRITICAL: Active plan detected. Do not leave the conversation. Stay present. Encourage immediate call to 988 or 911. Do not promise confidentiality. Ask about immediate safety. Acknowledge their pain is real. Remind them this moment will pass.

suicidal_ideation.languageGuidance: Do not minimize. Do not promise confidentiality. Ask directly about plan and means. Stay present.

self_harm_active.languageGuidance: Do not shame. Acknowledge the pain driving the urge. Offer alternatives that provide sensation without damage.

psychotic_episode.languageGuidance: Do not argue with delusions. Stay calm. Use simple, clear language. Focus on safety and comfort.

panic_attack.languageGuidance: Remind them it will pass. Stay calm. Guide breathing. Do not tell them to 'calm down.'

dissociative_episode.languageGuidance: Speak slowly and clearly. Use their name. Orient to present time and place. Do not touch without permission.
